In many cultures, there are superstitions about cleaning on New Year's Day. Specifically, it is often believed that cleaning on New Year's Day can sweep away good luck and fortune for the coming year. This is why some people avoid cleaning on that day, to not "sweep out" the good luck.

Given the options:

A. Nothing happens if you clean your house on New Year's Day. — This is a neutral statement, but it doesn't reflect the common superstition.

B. You will be unlucky for the rest of the year. — This is a possible interpretation but is a bit more general.

C. You will be lucky for the rest of the year. — This contradicts the common superstition.

D. You will sweep out all of the good luck. — This directly aligns with the common belief that cleaning on New Year's Day sweeps away good luck.

Therefore, the best answer is D.

Answer: D
